hasebe-ueda-problem-3-3-stationary-cauch.why: The statement matches the record's Proposition: support diameter at most 1, R>0, xi_R'(u_0)=0, xi_R''(u_0)>=0, conclusion xi_R(u_0)>=1. It keeps the same hypotheses and strength. The equality clause, R^2=3/4 with equal atoms at u_0±1/2, is the record's rigidity paragraph after translating u_0 to 0. I re-checked it: Phi/D is strictly concave in s and m(1+3m-D^2)>0 at s=0, so equality forces s=3/4, D=1 and m=1/4. The single atom delta_0 has F>=4/3, so it cannot carry equality. I also re-derived the closed forms for the pair weights, Phi, Psi, the (D,m) identities, and Lemmas A and B; they are correct. The proof text is the record's argument verbatim, with no invented steps. The draft gives the source title as 'Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions', with DOI and pages. The record abbreviates it as 'Unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions'. The draft's version is the published title of the same ALEA 15 (2018) paper and problem, so this is not a misnaming.

hasebe-ueda-problem-3-3-free-brownian-un.why: The draft weakens the record's theorem from t>=D^2 to t>D^2. The record establishes the endpoint from material it contains. A failure at t=D^2 needs a separating local minimum with xi_R(u_0)<=1/D^2. The Proposition then forces equality. The proved rigidity (equality case of the Proposition and Lemma B) makes mu a symmetric two-point law with R^2=3D^2/4. That law is unimodal at t=D^2 by the source's Example 2.1, which the record cites ('exact 4'; unimodal from t=4 on). So the bound holds at the record's strength, t>=D^2. The draft's own proof text already includes the rigidity paragraph. Also removed: the stray definition of classical convolution *, which plays no role.
hasebe-ueda-problem-3-3-free-brownian-un.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] This is the upper bound in the campaign answer to Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240). A probability measure is unimodal if, for some mode m, it is an atom at m plus an absolutely continuous measure whose density is nondecreasing to the left of m and nonincreasing to the right. Write boxplus for additive free convolution. For t>0 let S(0,t) be the centered semicircle law of variance t, with density sqrt(4t-x^2)/(2pi t) on |x|<=2sqrt(t). Let mu be compactly supported with positive diameter D=sup{|x-y|: x,y in supp(mu)}. Then mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=D^2. Proof route: by the source's Lemma 3.1 (Biane's description), non-unimodality at time t gives some R>0 and a separating local minimum u_0 of xi_R with xi_R(u_0)<=1/t. The stationary-kernel lower bound, rescaled to diameter D, gives xi_R(u_0)>=1/D^2, so t<=D^2. At t=D^2, equality would hold in that lower bound. This forces mu to be the symmetric two-point law with atoms at u_0±D/2 and R^2=3D^2/4, which is unimodal at t=D^2 by the source's Example 2.1. This is an unrefereed campaign result.

hasebe-ueda-problem-3-3-sharp-endpoint-a.why: The entry marks the endpoint t=D_mu^2, and with it C=1, as uncertified. The record does establish these: the endpoint follows from the proved rigidity plus Example 2.1, as explained for the theorem entry. The optimality half, failure for t<4 for the Bernoulli law on {-1,1}, is the source's Example 2.1. So C=1 is fully answered in the record. The only genuinely incomplete part is the 'only if' direction of the Corollary. That direction says t*(mu)=D_mu^2 only for symmetric two-point laws. The record supports it only by asserting that attaining t*(mu)=D_mu^2 needs a separating minimum at exactly 1/D_mu^2. When failures occur only at times t_n strictly below D_mu^2, that assertion needs a limiting or attainment argument that the record does not write out. The statement is corrected to separate what is proved from what is only claimed.
hasebe-ueda-problem-3-3-sharp-endpoint-a.statement: [campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked; the criterion reproduces the source's worked example, and every algebraic step was confirmed symbolically] Problem 3.3 of Takahiro Hasebe and Yuki Ueda's Large time unimodality for classical and free Brownian motions with initial distributions, ALEA 15 (2018), 353-374, DOI:10.30757/ALEA.v15-15 (arXiv:1710.08240), asks for the optimal universal C>0 such that mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=C D_mu^2 and every compactly supported probability measure mu. Here D_mu=sup{|x-y|: x,y in supp(mu)}, S(0,t) is the centered semicircle law of variance t, and boxplus is additive free convolution. The source proves C<=4. The record answers C=1. Sufficiency is the proved bound that mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for all t>=D_mu^2. Optimality is the source's Example 2.1: mu=(delta_{-1}+delta_1)/2, with D_mu=2, is not unimodal for any t<4=D_mu^2. Let t*(mu) be the least t_0 such that mu boxplus S(0,t) is unimodal for every t>=t_0. Then t*(mu)<=D_mu^2, and equality holds for every symmetric two-point law (equal weights at two points) by Example 2.1 and scaling. The record further claims (Corollary) that equality holds only for symmetric two-point laws. That direction rests on the record's unproved assertion that t*(mu)=D_mu^2 requires a separating local minimum of value exactly 1/D_mu^2, a limiting step not written out. It is retained here as a claim, not certified. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
